page.title: Generic OpenID Connect
page.subtitle: Federate McHarbor login to any compliant OpenID Connect provider — Auth0, Okta, Keycloak, AWS Cognito, Ping, ForgeRock, LemonLDAP, and many more. The plugin fetches <issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration at runtime to discover the authorization and token endpoints, then runs the standard OIDC authorization-code flow.
page.registerHint: Add a provider from the host's Settings > Security > Identity Providers page and pick "Generic OpenID Connect" as the provider_type.

help.issuer_url: The OIDC issuer URL — typically the base URL of your identity provider's user-facing portal (for example, https://login.example.com or https://your-tenant.auth0.com/). The plugin appends /.well-known/openid-configuration to discover the authorization endpoint, token endpoint, and JWKS URI.
help.client_id: OAuth client ID assigned by your IdP to the McHarbor application. Copy it from your IdP's application/client configuration screen.
help.client_secret: OAuth client secret issued by your IdP. Stored encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM).
help.scopes: Space-separated OAuth scopes. Defaults to 'openid profile email' which covers standard OIDC identity claims. Add 'groups' if your IdP exposes a group claim under that name (the host's group-mapping wizard reads the OIDC-asserted 'groups' claim).

guide.title: Set up Generic OpenID Connect in McHarbor
guide.subtitle: Register a confidential OAuth client in your IdP and grant it the right to read basic profile claims (and optionally groups).

step1.title: Open your IdP's application registration
step1.body: In your identity provider's admin console, navigate to Applications (or Clients / API Clients depending on the product) and create a new confidential web application. Pick a name like "McHarbor SSO" and choose the Web application type.

step2.title: Set the redirect URI
step2.body: Under Allowed Callback URLs / Redirect URIs, add the McHarbor callback URL shown on the provider edit page. The host appends /api/identity-providers/callback to your McHarbor base URL — copy it exactly to avoid silent auth-code mismatches.

step3.title: Create a client secret
step3.body: Generate a new client secret. Pick a sensible expiry (90 or 180 days) and set a calendar reminder. Copy the secret VALUE (not the secret ID) into the Client Secret field on the provider form. McHarbor stores it AES-256-GCM encrypted.

step4.title: Copy the Client ID
step4.body: From the application overview, copy the Client ID into the Client ID field on the provider form.

step5.title: Copy the Issuer URL
step5.body: The issuer URL is the base URL of your IdP — the same URL your users hit when they sign in. Common shapes: https://your-tenant.auth0.com/ (Auth0), https://your-org.okta.com/oauth2/default (Okta), https://keycloak.example.com/realms/master (Keycloak). Paste it into the Issuer URL field. The plugin will fetch <issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration to validate the configuration.

step6.title: Test the connection
step6.body: Back in McHarbor, click "Test connection" on the provider form. A green result means the OIDC discovery document resolved and the IdP accepted your credentials. You can now enable the provider and use "Sign in with <your IdP>" on the login page.
